What is the SI unit of force?\nnewton (N:
1) Force is defined through F = ma.
2) Units of mass times acceleration are kg times m/s^2, which is named the newton.
Answer: newton (N).
Why the others are wrong: The joule is the unit of energy, not force.
Which of the following is a contact forc:
1) A contact force requires the objects to touch.
2) Friction acts between surfaces in contact, while gravity, magnetic and electric forces act at a distance.
Answer: Friction.
Why the others are wrong: Gravity is a field force that acts without touching.
A box is pulled with 15 N to the right a:
1) Forces along a line add with signs, right positive.
2) Net = 15 - 5 = 10 N, positive so to the right.
Answer: 10 N to the right.
Why the others are wrong: Adding the magnitudes (20 N) ignores direction.
What does a free-body diagram show?\nOnl:
1) A free-body diagram isolates one object.
2) It draws only the forces that other things exert on that object, as arrows from a point.
Answer: Only the forces acting on one chosen object.
Why the others are wrong: Forces the object exerts on others belong on other diagrams.
Which pair of forces appears on the free:
1) Gravity pulls the book down, giving its weight.
2) The table pushes up on the book with the normal force.
3) The book is at rest, so these two are equal and opposite.
Answer: Weight downward and normal force upward.
Why the others are wrong: The book's push on the table acts on the table, not on the book.
Two forces of 3 N east and 4 N north act:
1) The forces are perpendicular, so use the Pythagorean theorem.
2) Net = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(25) = 5 N.
Answer: 5 N.
Why the others are wrong: Adding 3 + 4 = 7 N only works for forces in the same direction.
A 40 N force pulls a sled at 30 degrees:
1) The horizontal component is F cos(theta).
2) 40 x cos(30 degrees) = 40 x 0.866 = 34.6 N.
Answer: 34.6 N.
Why the others are wrong: 20 N uses sine, which gives the vertical component.
Forces of 8 N east, 6 N north and 2 N we:
1) East-west: 8 - 2 = 6 N east.
2) North-south: 6 N north.
3) Net = sqrt(6^2 + 6^2) = sqrt(72) = 8.5 N.
Answer: 8.5 N.
Why the others are wrong: 10 N comes from using 8 and 6 and ignoring the 2 N west force.
A net force has components of 30 N east:
1) The angle from east satisfies tan(theta) = north / east = 40 / 30.
2) theta = arctan(1.333) = 53 degrees, measured from east toward north.
Answer: 53 degrees north of east.
Why the others are wrong: 37 degrees comes from inverting the ratio, 30 / 40.
A rope pulls a crate with 50 N at 40 deg:
1) The vertical component is F sin(theta).
2) 50 x sin(40 degrees) = 50 x 0.643 = 32 N.
Answer: 32 N.
Why the others are wrong: 38 N (50 x cos 40) is the horizontal component.
According to Newton's first law, an obje:
1) The first law says velocity stays constant when the net force is zero.
2) So only a nonzero net external force can change the state of rest.
Answer: A net external force acts on it.
Why the others are wrong: Balanced forces together still give zero net force, so any force alone is not enough.
What is inertia?\nThe tendency of an obj:
1) Inertia is a property, not a force.
2) It describes how strongly an object resists a change in velocity, measured by mass.
Answer: The tendency of an object to resist changes in its motion.
Why the others are wrong: Inertia is not a force that pushes things along.
Which object has the greatest inertia?\n:
1) Inertia is measured by mass.
2) The largest mass listed is 10 kg.
Answer: A 10 kg bowling ball.
Why the others are wrong: Size or speed does not matter, only mass.
A bus brakes suddenly and passengers lur:
1) Before braking, passengers move with the bus.
2) The bus slows, but with no forward force the passengers keep their velocity, so they seem to lurch forward.
Answer: Inertia: passengers tend to keep moving at their original velocity.
Why the others are wrong: There is no real forward force; it is the lack of one.
A car moves at a constant velocity along:
1) Constant velocity means zero acceleration.
2) By the first law, zero acceleration means the net force is zero.
Answer: Zero.
Why the others are wrong: Motion alone does not require a net force.
A hockey puck slides on frictionless ice:
1) With no friction, the horizontal net force is zero.
2) By the first law, velocity stays constant at 5 m/s.
Answer: It keeps moving at 5 m/s in a straight line.
Why the others are wrong: Slowing down would need a force such as friction.

A car travels at constant velocity. Drag:
1) Constant velocity means net force is zero.
2) Forward force must balance the 800 N backward force, so it is 800 N.
Answer: 800 N.
Why the others are wrong: A larger forward force would make the car accelerate.
A 100 N sign hangs at rest from two equa:
1) Vertical equilibrium: 2T sin(30 degrees) = 100 N.
2) sin(30 degrees) = 0.5, so 2T x 0.5 = T = 100 N.
Answer: 100 N.

A 60 kg person stands in an elevator tha:
1) Constant velocity means zero acceleration and zero net force.
2) N = mg = 60 x 9.8 = 588 N.
Answer: 588 N.
Why the others are wrong: 708 N would apply if the elevator accelerated upward, but here only the velocity is constant.
Which equation expresses Newton's second:
1) The second law says acceleration is proportional to net force and inversely proportional to mass.
2) That gives a = F_net / m, the same as F_net = ma.
Answer: a = F_net / m.
Why the others are wrong: The other forms put mass or force in the wrong place.
A 1200 kg car experiences a net force of:
1) a = F_net / m.
2) a = 3000 / 1200 = 2.5 m/s^2.
Answer: 2.5 m/s^2.
Why the others are wrong: 0.4 comes from dividing mass by force.
The net force on an object doubles while:
1) a = F_net / m, so a is proportional to F_net.
2) Doubling F_net doubles a.
Answer: It doubles.
Why the others are wrong: Halving would happen if the mass doubled.
A 10 kg box is pushed with 50 N on a flo:
1) Net force = 50 - 20 = 30 N.
2) a = 30 / 10 = 3.0 m/s^2.
Answer: 3.0 m/s^2.
Why the others are wrong: 5.0 m/s^2 ignores friction.
A net force of 20 N gives an object an a:
1) m = F_net / a.
2) m = 20 / 4 = 5 kg.
Answer: 5 kg.
Why the others are wrong: 80 kg multiplies force and acceleration instead of dividing.
A 1000 kg car slows from 20 m/s to rest:
1) a = change in velocity / time = 20 / 5 = 4 m/s^2.
2) F = ma = 1000 x 4 = 4000 N.
Answer: 4000 N.
Why the others are wrong: 20000 N multiplies mass by speed, which is not a force.
The same net force acts on a 2 kg cart a:
1) a = F / m with equal F.
2) Ratio a(2 kg) / a(6 kg) = 6 / 2 = 3.
Answer: The 2 kg cart accelerates 3 times as much.
Why the others are wrong: Acceleration decreases as mass increases, so the heavier cart is slower to speed up.
A 0.15 kg ball is brought from rest to 4:
1) a = 40 / 0.010 = 4000 m/s^2.
2) F = ma = 0.15 x 4000 = 600 N.
Answer: 600 N.
Why the others are wrong: 4000 is the acceleration in m/s^2, not the force.
A 20 N force pushes a 3 kg block that to:
1) Treat both as one system: a = 20 / (3 + 2) = 4.0 m/s^2.
2) The 2 kg block alone needs F = ma = 2 x 4.0 = 8 N.
Answer: 8 N.
Why the others are wrong: 20 N is the applied force, which acts only on the first block.
A 500 kg rocket produces an upward thrus:
1) Weight = 500 x 9.8 = 4900 N downward.
2) Net force = 7400 - 4900 = 2500 N.
3) a = 2500 / 500 = 5.0 m/s^2.
Answer: 5.0 m/s^2.
Why the others are wrong: 14.8 m/s^2 divides thrust by mass without subtracting weight.
Which statement describes Newton's third:
1) If object A pushes on B, then B pushes back on A.
2) The two forces have equal size, opposite direction, and act on different objects.
Answer: Forces come in equal and opposite pairs acting on different objects.
Why the others are wrong: Pairs act on different objects so they do not cancel on one object.
What is the weight of a 60 kg person on:
1) Weight W = mg.
2) W = 60 x 9.8 = 588 N.
Answer: 588 N.
Why the others are wrong: 60 N is the mass number, not the force.
An astronaut travels from Earth to the M:
1) Mass measures matter and inertia, which do not depend on place.
2) Weight = mg, and g is smaller on the Moon, so weight decreases.
Answer: Weight.
Why the others are wrong: Mass is the same everywhere.
A hammer hits a nail with 200 N of force:
1) By Newton's third law the pair forces are equal.
2) The nail pushes back with 200 N in the opposite direction.
Answer: 200 N opposite to the hammer's force.
Why the others are wrong: The pair is always equal, even if one object is much smaller.
A 60 kg person is on the Moon where g =:
1) W = mg.
2) W = 60 x 1.6 = 96 N.
Answer: 96 N.
Why the others are wrong: 588 N is the weight on Earth.
Why do action and reaction forces not ca:
1) Cancelling requires forces on the same object.
2) The action acts on one object and the reaction on the other, so they cannot cancel.
Answer: They act on different objects.
Why the others are wrong: The forces are in fact equal in size.
An object weighs 490 N on Earth. What is:
1) m = W / g.
2) m = 490 / 9.8 = 50 kg.
Answer: 50 kg.
Why the others are wrong: 4802 kg multiplies instead of divides.
A truck hits a fly head-on. How does the:
1) The two forces are a third-law pair.
2) Pairs are always equal in magnitude.
Answer: They are equal in magnitude.
Why the others are wrong: The fly is damaged more only because its mass is small, so its acceleration is large.
A 70 kg person stands on a scale in an e:
1) Take up as positive: N - mg = ma.
2) N = m(g + a) = 70 x (9.8 + 2.0) = 70 x 11.8 = 826 N.
Answer: 826 N.
Why the others are wrong: 686 N is the weight at rest, which ignores the upward acceleration.
A 50 kg skater pushes an 80 kg skater wi:
1) By the third law the 80 kg skater pushes back on the 50 kg skater with 100 N.
2) a = F / m = 100 / 50 = 2.0 m/s^2.
Answer: 2.0 m/s^2.
Why the others are wrong: 1.25 m/s^2 is the acceleration of the 80 kg skater.
In which direction does kinetic friction:
1) Friction resists sliding between surfaces.
2) It therefore points opposite to the relative motion.
Answer: Opposite to the object's motion relative to the surface.
Why the others are wrong: Friction in the direction of motion would speed the object up.
Which formula gives the kinetic friction:
1) Friction is proportional to the normal force.
2) The constant of proportionality is the coefficient mu_k, so f = mu_k N.
Answer: f = mu_k N.
Why the others are wrong: Friction depends on the normal force, not directly on speed.
How does the maximum static friction usu:
1) It takes more force to start an object sliding than to keep it sliding.
2) So mu_s is usually larger than mu_k.
Answer: Maximum static friction is larger.
Why the others are wrong: Equal friction would mean no jolt when sliding begins.
A 20 kg crate slides on a level floor wi:
1) On a level floor N = mg = 20 x 9.8 = 196 N.
2) f = mu_k N = 0.30 x 196 = 58.8 N.
Answer: 58.8 N.
Why the others are wrong: 196 N is the normal force, not the friction.
A 10 kg block rests on a 30 degree incli:
1) Weight = 10 x 9.8 = 98 N.
2) N = mg cos(theta) = 98 x cos(30 degrees) = 98 x 0.866 = 84.9 N.
Answer: 84.9 N.

A block slides down a frictionless 30 de:
1) Only the component of weight along the slope acts: mg sin(theta).
2) a = g sin(30 degrees) = 9.8 x 0.5 = 4.9 m/s^2.
Answer: 4.9 m/s^2.
Why the others are wrong: 8.5 m/s^2 uses cosine instead of sine.
A 20 kg crate rests on a floor with mu_s:
1) N = mg = 20 x 9.8 = 196 N.
2) Max static friction = mu_s N = 0.50 x 196 = 98 N.
Answer: 98 N.
Why the others are wrong: 196 N is the normal force, not the friction limit.
A 20 kg crate is pushed horizontally wit:
1) Friction = 0.30 x 20 x 9.8 = 58.8 N.
2) Net force = 100 - 58.8 = 41.2 N.
3) a = 41.2 / 20 = 2.1 m/s^2.
Answer: 2.1 m/s^2.
Why the others are wrong: 5.0 m/s^2 ignores friction.
A 10 kg block slides down a 30 degree in:
1) Down-slope force = mg sin(30) = 49 N.
2) Friction = 0.20 x 84.9 = 17.0 N up the slope.
3) a = (49 - 17.0) / 10 = 3.2 m/s^2.
Answer: 3.2 m/s^2.

1) Constant speed means mg sin(theta) = mu_k mg cos(theta).
2) mu_k = tan(30 degrees) = 0.58.
Answer: 0.58.
